entities.name: Christian Mauritius of Königsegg-Rothenfels
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Count Christian Moritz von Königsegg und Rothfels (died 1778), a scion of an ancient Swabian noble family, rose to become a distinguished field marshal in the service of the Holy Roman Empire and the Habsburg Monarchy during the tumultuous mid-18th century. His career spanned the critical period of the War of the Austrian Succession (1740–1748) and the Seven Years' War (1756–1763), conflicts that fundamentally reshaped the balance of power in Central Europe and solidified Austria's position as a major continental force despite the rise of Prussia. Königsegg-Rothenfels served as a pivotal military commander under Empress Maria Theresa, contributing significantly to the professionalization and strategic deployment of Austrian forces against formidable opponents like Frederick the Great.

His military career included active command in key theaters. During the War of the Austrian Succession, he participated in campaigns in Bohemia and the Netherlands. Later, in the Seven Years' War, he held significant commands, notably as a corps commander under Prince Charles of Lorraine and later Field Marshal Leopold Joseph von Daun. He was present at the Battle of Kolín in 1757, a crucial Austrian victory over Frederick the Great's Prussians, and saw action at the subsequent Battle of Leuthen, where the Austrian forces suffered a devastating defeat. Despite the latter, his long service and consistent leadership earned him respect within the Habsburg military hierarchy.
